## Quick Start

### With an AI coding agent

For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes
claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes
```

To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a
terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select
**Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use
`/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx)
for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration.

For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use:

```bash
npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes
```

> The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 7 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`.
>
> `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill.

Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames
checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a
project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and
overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started).

Try a prompt like:

> Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music.

The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills.

install.installSection:
## Quick start

### Linux and macOS (two commands, no root)

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
ai-memory setup
```

`install.sh` downloads the release for your OS and CPU, checks it against the
release's published SHA-256 checksum (it refuses to install without a match),
and links `~/.local/bin/ai-memory`. `ai-memory setup` then creates the data
directory with a bearer token in an owner-only file, starts a per-user service
(systemd `--user` or a launchd LaunchAgent), and wires MCP, hooks and Agent
Skills for every agent it finds, or the ones you name with `--agent`. It shows
the plan, with where it found each agent, and asks first: answer `y`, or type
the numbers of the agents to wire. `--plan` prints the plan and changes
nothing, `--web` shows the plan as a page in your browser and applies the agents
you tick there, `--yes` skips the question, and running it again changes nothing.
Afterwards, restart your agents and ask one of them "What do you remember
about this project?" to see it answer through ai-memory. Details, the environment
variables and how to verify the script before running it are in
[`docs/install.md`](docs/install.md#one-step-native-install-installsh--ai-memory-setup).
An AI agent installing ai-memory for you can follow
[`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md).

Claude Code and Codex users can wire their agent as a marketplace plugin
instead (the binary is still installed as above):

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add akitaonrails/ai-memory && claude plugin install ai-memory@ai-memory
codex plugin marketplace add akitaonrails/ai-memory && codex plugin add ai-memory@ai-memory
```

Codex then asks you to trust the hooks in `/hooks`. See
[Marketplace plugins](docs/install.md#marketplace-plugins).

### Windows (two commands, no admin)

In PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
ai-memory setup
```

`install.ps1` checks the release zip against its published SHA-256 checksum,
unpacks it under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ai-memory` and adds that directory
to your user `PATH`. `ai-memory setup` then does what it does on Linux and
macOS, with a logon entry in place of the service: the server starts when you
sign in, with no console window, and restarts if it fails. Details and the
other Windows setups (WSL2, Docker Desktop, a real Windows service) are in
[`docs/windows.md`](docs/windows.md).

**Option A: Claude Code Plugin (recommended)**

From within Claude Code, first add the marketplace:
```
/plugin marketplace add forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills

/plugin install andrej-karpathy-skills@karpathy-skills
```

This installs the guidelines as a Claude Code plugin, making the skill available across all your projects.

New project:
```bash
curl -o CLAUDE.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills/main/CLAUDE.md

```bash
echo "" >> CLAUDE.md

```
